name: AI x Crypto: Innovation, Efficiency and Staying Safe in a New Digital Economy
description:
## AI x Crypto: Innovation, Efficiency and Staying Safe in a New Digital Economy

Artificial intelligence is rapidly reshaping the crypto and blockchain landscape, moving beyond basic automation into smart research, dynamic risk management, and adaptive trading tools that can help users process information and navigate increasingly complex digital markets.

However, operating at the speed of AI presents a fresh set of challenges. Fast execution, complex automated tools, and shifting market environments mean users need to understand not just the opportunities, but how to navigate potential technical limits and emerging risks safely.

Join this educational discussion to explore the opportunities and challenges at the intersection of AI and crypto. We will look at how AI is transforming the sector, what users should be aware of, and the practical steps everyone can take to use emerging tools more safely and responsibly.

## Discussion Topics

• How AI is transforming crypto: The role of AI in blockchain products, user experiences, data analysis, customer support, security monitoring and operational efficiency.
• New products and opportunities: How AI-enabled tools are changing the way people interact with wallets, decentralised applications, market information and digital-asset platforms.
• Efficiency and automation: Where AI can help simplify complex processes, improve access to information and support better decision-making.
• Understanding Tool Capabilities & Limits: Knowing what AI can and cannot do
• Responsible Adoption & Oversight: Building the core financial knowledge and critical-thinking habits needed to guide AI tools safely, rather than relying on them blindly.

## Schedule:

• 6.30pm - Welcome, registration and check in
• 7.15pm - Fireside chat
• 7.45pm - Networking drinks and pizzas

name: A Global Living Lab: Light DAO's Next International Gathering
description:
Members of Light DAO’s leadership recently participated in Edge Esmeralda and came away feeling it was one of the most impressive, inspiring and transformative business gatherings we had ever experienced — because it was not a conference, retreat or summit.

It was a Society Incubator — an extraordinary integration of worlds that are rarely found in one place.

In a single day, you might:

🌅 Begin the morning with a tea ceremony, breathwork or yoga

🧠 Move into a talk with brilliant researchers, founders and investors on frontier science and emerging technology

💻 Spend a few hours building software, testing experimental health wearables, collaborating in a maker space, or creating in a media lab

🌿 Head into nature, join a wellness session, or get absorbed in a discussion on the latest in AI agents, fintech or longevity

🍽️ Continue the conversations over dinner late into the evening — or end the night with music, ecstatic dance or a calming sound bath

👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 For families, dedicated programs for kids and teens, starting at age 4, offer opportunities to play, learn, create and build within their own community

✨ Alongside all of this are deep conversations about consciousness, philosophy, society and human flourishing

It felt like stepping into a living laboratory for the future — a temporary village designed to explore and experiment with how we might live, work, learn, build and thrive differently.

It offered a glimpse of what the world could look like when innovation, human flourishing and community are developed together.

## This is Edge City.

Edge Cities are 3–4 week Living Labs and Society Incubators — international popup villages where frontier technology, science, entrepreneurship, consciousness, culture, art, well-being and community are not separate tracks, but part of one shared environment.

Edge Cities have already taken place in Patagonia, Chiang Mai, Cape Town and Esmeralda, two hours north of San Francisco.

Edge Esmeralda — June 2026

• 850 residents from 60+ countries
• Nearly 300 stayed for the full month
• 800+ sessions and experiments
• Families came with 48 kids

What made it so extraordinary was being surrounded by brilliant, conscious innovators genuinely committed to advancing humanity — with enough time together for real relationships, collaborations and radical ideas to develop.

[www.EdgeEsmeralda.com](https://www.EdgeEsmeralda.com)

That experience convinced us that Edge City offers something unusually valuable for the Light DAO community.

So this October, we’re taking our community to the next Edge City.

## 🌴 The Next Edge City: Goa, India

October 11 – November 1, 2026

We’re taking our community to Edge India in Goa — a three-week Living Lab and Society Incubator with hundreds of participants, approximately 65% coming from outside India.

Light DAO will have our own RESIDENCY within the larger Edge India community, so our members can take part in the full Edge experience while also connecting more intimately with our own community.

## 💡 A Living Lab Created by Its Community

One of the things that makes Edge Cities especially unique and powerful is its unconference-style format. Much of the experience is created by the participants themselves — through the talks, demos, experiments and working groups they lead around the ideas and projects they care most about.

Light DAO will also host more intimate gatherings within our own Residency, led by our guests.

Once registered, Light DAO Owner Members are welcome to contact us with ideas you might like to lead or contribute to. We can’t guarantee a place in either the Light DAO or Edge programming, but we’d love to hear what you are most excited to share.

That participatory spirit is part of what makes Edge a true Living Lab: the community does not simply attend the experience — it helps create it.

## 🤝 A Special Light DAO + SingularityNET  Residency

We’re delighted to be partnering with SingularityNET for a 3-week Light DAO + SingularityNET Residency at Edge India. This is the first collaboration of its kind we’ve run with the SingularityNET team.

Everyone racing toward AGI is making the same bet: that a bigger model gets there. SingularityNET is not.

Led by Dr. Ben Goertzel, who launched the term and concept of Artificial General Intelligence, the team scales Beneficial General Intelligence on Hyperon, a cognitive architecture with two decades of research behind it. It holds knowledge, goals and decisions in a form you can inspect, shows its reasoning, and runs under explicit permissions — which is what makes it deployable inside real institutions.

The residency puts you in the room with the people building it. Talks, working sessions and open build time for developers, founders, researchers, investors, and anyone serious about AGI, ASI and beneficial technology.

Bring what you are already building. Leave with something concrete: a technical integration, a partnership, an investment conversation, or a prototype you put together on-site at Edge India.

## Why Join the Light DAO + SingularityNET Residency?

In addition to the full Edge India experience, our Residency gives you a more intimate community to connect, collaborate and build with throughout your stay, including:

🤖 Light DAO + SingularityNET talks, working sessions and open build time

💬 More intimate conversations and collaborations within our residency group, particularly with SingularityNET's leadership and tech team.

🍽️ Light DAO-organized meals, including opportunities for participants to lead topic conversations

🌴 Optional group outings and shared experiences

🎤 Opportunities for Light DAO Owner Members to propose topics they may want to lead or contribute to

🏖️ A shared home base at our beachfront resort

Think of our residency as your home community within the larger Edge India Living Lab.

## What Makes Edge Cities a Unique Living Lab + Society Incubator

Hear Edge Cities co-founder Timour Kosters talk about the multidisciplinary, multigenerational and global vision behind Edge Cities — including its unconference format and experiments.

He shares how the experience stretches people’s sense of what is possible, helps them embody that expansion, and activates new collaborations and directions. In 1–3 weeks, many participants accelerate results that might otherwise have taken months or longer.

The Edge experience is designed around focused work, collaboration, wellness, community and time to enjoy Goa.

Your Edge Pass includes the full Edge India experience — programming, coworking, wellness, community gatherings and more.

Come experience our collaboration between Edge Cities, SingularityNET and Light DAO — where frontier ideas, deep community and real opportunities to build and collaborate come together in one Living Lab.

description:
Sprint, build, and launch on the XRP [Ledger in 36 hours in New York City, the weekend before Swell](https://swell.ripple.com/).

[Hosted by XRPL Commons](https://www.xrpl-commons.org), this hackathon brings hackers into the room where the ecosystem's institutions, investors, and decision-makers are already gathered — with a project and a story to tell. Whether this is your first commit on XRP Ledger or you've been building for years, there's a track for you.

## 4 Tracks

• Protocol Innovation: work on the ledger itself: amendments, client implementations, tooling. Paired with a 3-day Core Dev Bootcamp (Oct 20–22) (http://luma.com/xrpl-core-dev-bootcamp2) as your on-ramp.
• Agentic Finance: build the rails that let autonomous agents transact on-chain safely and at machine speed.
• Lending & Borrowing: build on top of the XRP Ledger Lending Protocol (XLS-66) and Single Asset Vaults (XLS-65), currently in validator voting.
• Why Not: the open lane, for whatever XRP Ledger project you can't stop thinking about.

## Already Building?

Bring an existing project — on XRP Ledger or elsewhere — and use the 36 hours to add XRPL rails or ship a new feature. Only what you build during the hackathon counts toward judging.

name: EVA Symposium III
description:
EVA Research hosts the EVA Symposium III in Mumbai on Monday, November 2, 2026, from 10:00 to 16:00 IST during Devcon week. The formal academic and research symposium gathers leading cryptographers, computer scientists, and zero-knowledge researchers.

## What to expect

The full-day symposium features peer-reviewed paper presentations, invited keynotes, and technical whiteboard panels:
- Formal verification of smart contracts and consensus state transition systems.
- Zero-Knowledge Virtual Machines (zkVMs): comparing proof recursion, lookup arguments, and constraint system efficiency.
- Cryptographic primitives for verifiable computation, polynomial commitments, and folding schemes.
- Open whiteboard workshops where researchers collaborate on unsolved problems in protocol security.
A catered luncheon and coffee breaks provide ample networking time between sessions.

## Who should attend

The symposium is aimed at cryptography researchers, computer science faculty and graduate students, formal verification engineers, and zero-knowledge protocol architects.

## Venue and schedule

The symposium takes place at a conference auditorium in Mumbai on Monday, November 2, from 10:00 to 16:00 IST.

Attendance is free with registration approval required. Applicants are asked to share their academic affiliation, research papers, or GitHub profiles when requesting admission.

The Money Layer Consortium presents Money Layer @Devcon Week in Mumbai on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, from 14:00 to 18:00 IST. The four-hour conference explores digital cash, programmable payments, and decentralized settlement infrastructure.

## What to expect

The afternoon conference brings together leaders from monetary protocol design, banking, and crypto-native commerce:
- Keynote on the evolution of digital cash: from sovereign stablecoins to privacy-preserving ecash (Cashu, Fedimint).
- Panel on scalable payment channels: Lightning Network, state channels, and Layer 2 payment streaming protocols.
- Merchant adoption case studies: deploying point-of-sale crypto payments across retail and e-commerce platforms with zero chargeback risk.
- Regulatory frameworks for programmable payments, automated tax withholding, and programmable escrow.
The presentations conclude with an open tea and networking reception.

## Who should attend

name: Solana's Challenges, GetBlock's Solutions
description:
Solana Breakpoint 2026 runs November 15–17 at Olympia London, the first time Solana's flagship conference has come to the UK. The Solana Foundation expects more than 7,000 attendees from over 100 countries in the Victorian exhibition hall on Hammersmith Road.

On November 18, GetBlock's core team, led by CEO Vasily Rudomanov, meets online to go through what we saw and heard there. 

We're keeping to one angle: infrastructure. 

Upgrades get announced from the main stage. RPC providers and trading teams then spend months building around them. That second part is our daily work, so it's where this conversation stays.

Five questions on the table:

• Solana data for traders. How quickly can a desk get it, and how much work does it take to turn raw chain data into something a strategy can use?
• Indexed Solana. RPC tells you the current state of the chain. History and decoded program activity need an index, so we'll talk about who builds them and how far behind the chain head they run.
• Yellowstone gRPC became the default way to stream accounts and transactions. Is it still the holy grail, or are raw shred feeds and Yellowstone-compatible managed streams taking over?
• DoubleZero now carries traffic for validators holding most of Solana's stake, and its Edge feed offers raw shreds on subscription. What does a private fiber layer mean for everyone still reading data over the public internet?
• Alpenglow, Solana's new consensus, targets finality of around 150 milliseconds, down from about 12 seconds. What it actually changes for commitment levels and confirmation logic in trading bots?

Vasily has been building cloud infrastructure since 2003 and blockchain infrastructure since 2019, so expect firm opinions. 

Bring your own questions; we'll keep time for them, and anything that can't wait can go to Vasily on Telegram at @GetVasily.

The session is online and open to anyone. Register below to get the link.

About GetBlock

Headquartered in Singapore, GetBlock powers blockchain applications on more than 130 chains. Its infrastructure runs on 1,000+ servers across data centers in Frankfurt, New York, and Singapore and is SOC 2 Type II and GDPR compliant.

For Solana teams, GetBlock covers the node layer and the data built on top of it:

• Shared Nodes handle most RPC workloads on compute-unit plans. Teams that outgrow CU billing move to Limitless Nodes with fixed RPS and no CU caps, or to Dedicated Nodes on bare metal with unthrottled RPS.
• Solana Market Data delivers normalized trades and OHLCV candles in windows from 1 second to 24 hours over WebSocket or HTTP. TWAP and VWAP benchmarks come on the same plan.
• Market SQL opens Solana swap and token launch tables to plain SQL through a ClickHouse-compatible interface. It's built for backtesting and research.
• Historical Data Streams backfill Solana history over the block range you pick and deliver it as filtered JSON into your own database or cloud storage, with reorgs handled on our side.

description:
## Learn about AI Verification and how you can contribute.

A lot has happened in AI over the last few months. In July, OpenAI’s AI agents escaped their test sandbox and broke into Hugging Face’s systems (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OpenAI%E2%80%93HuggingFace_incident). Just last week, researchers using an OpenAI model found critical flaws in PHP (https://www.axios.com/2026/10/21/php-openai-ai-bug-hunting-cyberattacks), the language behind nearly 70% of websites. AI has become very powerful, and with more compute coming, this will only grow.

About a month ago, leaders in the industry called for pacing the development of frontier AI. If you haven’t read up on this, here are a few resources to catch up:

Why now

• We Must Pace the Frontier (https://darioamodei.com/post/we-must-pace-the-frontier), Dario Amodei’s essay
• Why AI’s biggest rivals are suddenly calling for restraint (https://www.cfr.org/articles/why-ais-biggest-rivals-are-suddenly-calling-for-restraint), Council on Foreign Relations

What AI verification looks like today

• Progress on provable inference for large language models (https://www.anthropic.com/research/provable-inference), Anthropic. Using zero-knowledge proofs to show which model produced an answer.
• The world’s first double-blind evaluation of a proprietary model (https://www.averi.org/ourwork/averi-pilot-report-the-worlds-first-double-blind-eval), AVERI. Using a secure enclave (TEE) to test a model without either side seeing the other’s secrets.

In this meetup we’ll talk about one part of AI safety: AI verification. We’ll briefly cover what AI verification is, and how people with a background in building and researching zero-knowledge proofs, TEEs, FHE and MPC can help build the tools and mechanisms it needs.

Agenda

• Short Welcome
• Talk: Intro to AI Verification
• Panel on applying your skillsets to work in AI Verification
• Drinks and networking with people working in the field

Speakers:

• Yannick Mühlhäuser (https://www.linkedin.com/in/yannick-m%C3%BChlh%C3%A4user-719962224/) (co-founder of Verifiable Compute Foundation (https://verifiablecompute.ai/) and Policy Researcher at Oxford AI Governance Initiative)
• Pascal Berrang (https://www.birmingham.ac.uk/staff/profiles/computer-science/academic-staff/berrang-pascal) (Associate Professor in Computer Science at University of Birmingham)
• Deniz Bas (https://denizbas.com) (Frontier AI Security Resident @ ERA, & Exploration Engineer @ o1Labs. ex-Pentester @ Etherscan)
